comparison: Both address resolution claims (C1, C78, C79). OpenEval accepts the resolution determination with explanation of discrepancy between 4.6 Å and 5.3 Å estimates. Peer reviewers questioned the 4.6 Å claim as likely overestimated, expecting actual resolution 'no better than 5 Å' and requesting additional validation to reduce over-fitting risk.

Both evaluate quasi-equivalent structural variations (C32-C37). OpenEval finds quantitative measurements reasonable with appropriate caveats about C38 speculation. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this as 'A technical highlight' and affirmed the findings about domain positions and molecular contacts, noting merit of cryo-EM over crystallization artifacts.

Both address CHK-152 neutralization mechanism (C2, C60-C61, C63-C64, C73). OpenEval finds mechanism well-supported by structural and functional data despite unpublished fusion-blocking observations. Peer reviewers acknowledged 'new insights...into how the capsid interacts with neutralizing antibodies' as 'potentially of medical interest' without raising concerns about these mechanistic interpretations.

Both evaluate receptor-blocking mechanisms (C3, C57-C59, C65-C67, C72). OpenEval finds structural mapping and stoichiometric arguments logically sound with functional validation. Peer reviewers accepted antibody-binding analysis as part of manuscript's contribution to understanding neutralizing antibodies, with no specific concerns raised about binding site mapping or proposed mechanisms.

Both address Fab complex structures and resolution (C54-C56). OpenEval finds 15 Å cryo-EM resolution sufficient for localization and domain movement detection, with high-quality crystal structures. Peer reviewers acknowledged insights into antibody interactions, requested additional quality-of-fit figures but did not challenge resolution estimates or structural observations.

Both evaluate VLP architectural features (C15-C16, C26-C31). OpenEval finds structural observations consistent with known alphavirus structures and appropriate for 5.3 Å resolution. Peer reviewers acknowledged manuscript as 'a major advance' with 'new insights at much higher resolution' without raising concerns about these specific structural observations.

Both address NCP modeling and contact analysis (C41-C47). OpenEval finds approach appropriate given resolution and sequence similarity, with quantitative validation. Peer reviewers did not challenge NCP modeling or inter-molecular contact analysis, accepting findings while suggesting more focused presentation on novel aspects.

Both evaluate comparative structural analysis with VEEV (C50-C53). OpenEval finds comparison valid with interesting observations about conserved proteins showing larger changes. Peer reviewers explicitly requested authors 'focus more on the structural differences between the two viruses,' indicating they accept the comparative analysis as valid and important.

Both address stoichiometric neutralization requirements (C68-C71). OpenEval finds logical arguments sound with functional validation from neutralization data. Peer reviewers did not challenge these mechanistic interpretations, implicitly accepting proposed mechanisms as part of insights into antibody interactions that are 'potentially of medical interest.'

Both evaluate spike differences and pH-sensing residues (C38-C40). OpenEval finds residue interactions observable at 5.3 Å with appropriate caveats about interaction geometry uncertainty. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about these structural observations or functional interpretations, implicitly accepting them as part of detailed structural analysis.

Both address VLP validity as model system (C74-C75). OpenEval finds background information properly supported by citations. Peer reviewers evaluated manuscript based on VLP structures without raising concerns about validity of using VLPs as surrogates for infectious virus, implicitly accepting this experimental approach.

Both address extensive background claims (C4-C13, C17-C25, C48, C49, C62). OpenEval finds background information properly supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. Peer reviewers did not challenge any background claims, implicitly accepting contextual information that provides scientific foundation for the study.

Both address technical details about data collection (C76-C77, C80). OpenEval finds methodological details comprehensive with appropriate quality metrics. Peer reviewers did not challenge technical details about data collection or particle numbers, though they questioned resolution assessment methods and requested additional validation.

Both address crystallographic parameters for Fab structures (C81-C85). OpenEval finds crystal structures provide high-quality atomic models with appropriate validation. Peer reviewers did not dispute reported crystallographic results or technical parameters, though they requested quality-of-fit figures to verify results.

OpenEval evaluated transmembrane helix arrangement (C49) as supported by density and modeling. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found, though C49 appears in peer R12 as part of broader background claims that were accepted.
